1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# tests/e2e.sh must print kernel_cycles -- the vsim mcycle delta over the
3	# measured region (vsim drain - QEMU1 drain, offset 624) -- for both
4	# trigger modes (marker, pc), so the `./andesim run --mode hybrid
5	# --trigger marker|pc` surface carries the cycle figure.
6	#
7	# Fixture: rt_c_v_matmul.elf (marked RVV GEMM). Marker mode uses the
8	# ROI marker HINTs in the source; PC mode resolves the boundaries
9	# from the binary itself (no planted _hybrid_*_pc labels).
10	#
11	# Manual TDD smoke test (runs real QEMU+vsim round-trips); not wired into
12	# scripts/run_e2e.sh.
13	
14	set -uo pipefail
15	
16	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
17	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)
18	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul
19	
20	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/log.sh"
21	. "$ROOT/setup.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
22	
23	# Resolve the PC immediately after `jal vmatmul_kernel` in the marked
24	# GEMM ELF; that's the PC at which vsim drains for PC mode (ROI_END).
25	# Recompiling the fixture relocates this address, so we derive it from
26	# objdump every run.
27	resolve_post_jal_pc() {
28	  local elf="$1"
29	  "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump" -d "$elf" \
30	    | awk '
31	        /jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/ { matched = 1; next }
32	        matched { sub(":", "", $1); printf "0x%s\n", $1; exit }
33	      '
34	}
35	
36	check_mode() {
37	  local mode="$1"; shift
38	  local out rc n
39	  out=$(env FIXTURE="$FIXTURE" TRIGGER_MODE="$mode" EXPECT_RC=0 TIMEOUT=120 \
40	        "$@" bash "$ROOT/tests/e2e.sh" 2>&1)
41	  rc=$?
42	  if [ "$rc" -eq 77 ]; then
43	    echo "[skip] $mode round-trip skipped (rc=77, e.g. toolchain missing)"
44	    return 0
45	  fi
46	  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$out"; fail "$mode round-trip did not exit 0 (rc=$rc)"; }
47	  n=$(echo "$out" | sed -nE 's/.*kernel_cycles\][[:space:]]*([0-9]+).*/\1/p' | head -1)
48	  { [ -n "$n" ] && [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; } \
49	    || { echo "$out"; fail "$mode: kernel_cycles not a positive integer (got '${n:-}')"; }
50	  echo "[ok] $mode round-trip printed kernel_cycles=$n"
51	}
52	
53	check_mode marker
54	
55	if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
56	  echo "[skip] pc round-trip: HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset (run \`source ./setup.sh\`)"
57	else
58	  POST_JAL_PC=$(resolve_post_jal_pc "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf")
59	  [ -n "$POST_JAL_PC" ] || fail "could not resolve post-jal PC for vmatmul_kernel"
60	  check_mode pc ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END="$POST_JAL_PC"
61	fi
62	
63	echo "PASS test_kernel_cycles"
64

---
commit 8019029617977163d9e086fc7a258a24944d402c
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Wed Jul 8 11:55:18 2026 +0800

    refactor!: remove the vsim->QEMU2 handback -- the run ends at the vsim drain
    
    The hybrid flow is now 2-phase: QEMU1 drains on the trigger, then vsim
    resumes, runs the region, and drains -- the reported cycle figure is the
    vsim mcycle delta, so the QEMU2 gdb-stub resume leg added no measurement
    value and only widened the failure surface. This single removal commit
    deletes the QEMU2 leg where it actually lived in this tree: the four
    QEMU2/gdbstub test doubles under tests/drivers/ (qemu_silent_stub.py,
    rt_gdbstub_timeout.sh, rt_no_qemu_binary.sh, rt_pty_handback.sh) are
    git-rm'd, keeping only rt_corrupt_state.sh. tests/e2e.sh becomes a 2-step
    QEMU1->vsim harness: it drops vsim's --qemu-binary spawn, the EXPECT_RC
    knob, and the phase-3 assertion, and instead gates on vsim exiting 200 on
    a clean drain. The drain-only plugin carries no apply-state/resume path,
    so hybrid_handoff.c needs no change.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
15:    QEMU1->vsim harness: it drops vsim's --qemu-binary spawn, the EXPECT_RC
37:-#   EXPECT_RC       Final exit code to assert (default 0).
45:-EXPECT_RC="${EXPECT_RC:-0}"
99:-if [ "$RC" != "$EXPECT_RC" ]; then
100:-  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: expected exit $EXPECT_RC, got $RC"
